styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old Town lanes, Art Nouveau streets and markets.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Medieval Riga, occupation museums and Soviet traces.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Parks, the Daugava and a day at Jūrmala beach.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, squares and museums. Noisy at night and cobblestones are rough; ask for a quiet room.
Art Nouveau district and good cafés; 10–15 minutes on foot to the Old Town. Good transport links.
Quiet wooden-house streets across the river, near the market and parks. Cheaper; cross the bridge to the centre.
Local, budget-friendly neighbourhood with the central market nearby. Simple tram or bus ride to the centre.

food: Try Latvian dishes: grey peas with bacon, rye bread, and smoked fish. Lunch menus are the best value.
Riga Central Market: old zeppelin hangars with cheese, berries, smoked meat and cheap snacks.
Book ahead for popular Old Town restaurants in summer; walk-ins fill up after 19:00.
Lido is a good budget canteen chain for hearty local food; pay by weight.
Black balsam is the local herbal liqueur. Sip it slowly or try it in a cocktail.
more_time: Swap an afternoon for Jūrmala: seasonal boat May to September, €15–20, about 2.5 hours, or a short train ride.
Add the Art Nouveau district walk on Alberta iela and the nearby museum if you like architecture.
History fans can add a half-day at the occupation museum or the Soviet-era sights outside the centre.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Old Town, the Art Nouveau streets and the market at an easy pace; add a third for Jūrmala or a museum day.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 0°C and lows around -4°C. Pack a warm coat and boots; expect about 14 rain or snow days.
February: still cold, highs near 2°C. Short daylight; plan indoor sights and warm cafés.
March: slowly milder, highs around 6°C, but nights stay below freezing. Bring layers.
April: highs near 11°C, lows around 2°C. Showers are common; a light rain jacket helps.
May: pleasant at 17°C highs. Good for walking; evenings still cool at around 7°C.
June: mild and bright, highs near 22°C. Long days; pack a light layer for evenings at 13°C.
July: warmest month, highs around 22°C, but the wettest with about 15 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
August: similar to July, highs near 22°C and about 13 rain days. Good for parks and day trips.
September: cooling to 18°C highs. Fewer crowds; bring a jacket for 11°C evenings.
October: highs near 11°C and about 14 rain days. Grey and damp; indoor plans are safer.
November: cold and dark, highs around 5°C. About 13 rain days; warm waterproof shoes.
December: highs near 2°C, lows around -2°C, about 15 rain or snow days. Christmas market weather; dress warmly.

climate_guide.summary: Baltic climate: cold winters, mild summers and rain in every month. Summer days are long; winter days are short.

items.title: Best time: June to August
items.text: Highs around 22°C and long daylight. The busiest and priciest season; book ahead.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 9–15 rain days every month. July and December are wettest; May is driest.

items.title: Winter is cold
items.text: January highs near 0°C and lows around -4°C. Snow is possible; wear a warm coat and boots.

items.title: Short winter days
items.text: November to February has little daylight. Plan indoor sights and start early.

items.title: Shoulder seasons are quiet
items.text: April–May and September–October are cheaper with fewer crowds, but pack rain gear.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Add a warm hat and gloves from November to March.

transit.best: Walk the Old Town and centre; use trams and buses for longer hops, and ride apps at night.

modes.text: No metro in Riga. Don't plan around rail inside the city.

Trams, buses and trolleybuses by Rigas Satiksme: single fare €1.50 valid 90 minutes with transfers. Buy via Mobilly, Narvesen or ticket machines and scan the vehicle QR code. 24-hour pass €5, 3-day €8, 5-day €10; free on some holidays.
Bolt, Panda Taxi and Red Cab work well. Avoid hailing random street taxis.
Not advised: traffic and parking fees up to €8/hour in the Old Town.
Best way to see the Old Town, but cobblestones are rough. Bikes and e-scooters are common April to September.
Seasonal boat to Jūrmala runs May to September, €15–20, about 2.5 hours.
